title: Cards and poker hands
description:
Model a deck of playing cards with enums and records, and rank five-card poker hands. Each type goes in its own file, named after it, as in any Java project: `Suit.java`, `Rank.java`, `Card.java`, `Deck.java`, `Category.java`, `HandValue.java` and `Poker.java`.

```java
enum Suit { CLUBS, DIAMONDS, HEARTS, SPADES }           // symbols C, D, H, S
enum Rank { TWO, THREE, ..., TEN, JACK, QUEEN, KING, ACE }   // symbols 2-9, T, J, Q, K, A
record Card(Rank rank, Suit suit)                       // toString: "AS", "TH", "2C"; static Card parse(String)
class Deck                                              // a full 52-card deck
enum Category { HIGH_CARD, PAIR, TWO_PAIR, THREE_OF_A_KIND, STRAIGHT, FLUSH, FULL_HOUSE, FOUR_OF_A_KIND, STRAIGHT_FLUSH }
record HandValue(Category category, List<Rank> tiebreak) implements Comparable<HandValue>
class Poker
    static List<Card> parseHand(String text)            // "AS KD 7H 7C 2S"
    static HandValue evaluate(List<Card> five)
    static int compare(String hand1, String hand2)      // positive if hand1 wins, negative if hand2 wins, 0 for a tie
```

**Cards and deck**
- `Card.parse("QH")` gives the queen of hearts; anything else (wrong length, unknown symbol) throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Symbols are upper case.
- `new Deck()` has 52 different cards in order: suits in enum order, and within each suit ranks from two to ace. `size()`, `deal()` (removes and returns the top card, the first one; `IllegalStateException` when empty) and `shuffle(Random random)` (use `Collections.shuffle(list, random)`).

**Evaluating a hand** (exactly 5 different cards, else `IllegalArgumentException`):
- Categories from lowest to highest as in the enum. A **straight** is five consecutive ranks; the ace can also be low in `A 2 3 4 5` (a five-high straight). A **flush** is five cards of one suit.
- `tiebreak` lists the ranks that decide between two hands of the same category, most important first: ranks ordered by how many times they occur (more first), then by rank (higher first). So `7H 7C AS KD 2S` (a pair) gives `[SEVEN, ACE, KING, TWO]`, and `KS KH 4D 4C KC` (full house) gives `[KING, FOUR]`. For straights and straight flushes it is just the highest card, with `FIVE` for the ace-low straight.
- `HandValue.compareTo` compares the category first, then the tiebreak lists rank by rank.

starter.Suit.java: enum Suit { CLUBS, DIAMONDS, HEARTS, SPADES }
starter.Rank.java: enum Rank { TWO, THREE, FOUR, FIVE, SIX, SEVEN, EIGHT, NINE, TEN, JACK, QUEEN, KING, ACE }
starter.Category.java: enum Category { HIGH_CARD, PAIR, TWO_PAIR, THREE_OF_A_KIND, STRAIGHT, FLUSH, FULL_HOUSE, FOUR_OF_A_KIND, STRAIGHT_FLUSH }

solution.Category.java: enum Category { HIGH_CARD, PAIR, TWO_PAIR, THREE_OF_A_KIND, STRAIGHT, FLUSH, FULL_HOUSE, FOUR_OF_A_KIND, STRAIGHT_FLUSH }

hints: Give `Suit` and `Rank` a `symbol` field and a static `of(char)` that searches `values()`; then `Card.parse` and `toString` are one line each.

List the distinct ranks by count descending, then rank descending: loop over the counts from 4 down to 1, and for each, over the ranks from ace down to two, adding every rank with that count. That single list gives the category (look at the first two counts) and the tiebreak at once.
Five distinct ranks are a straight when the highest minus the lowest is 4, or when they are exactly A, 5, 4, 3, 2.
requirements: `Suit`, `Rank` and `Category` are enums with the symbol as a field where needed; `Card` and `HandValue` are records.
`evaluate` counts ranks once (an array or `EnumMap`) and derives every category from those counts and a flush check.
stretch: Add `best(List<Card> seven)`, which finds the best five-card hand among seven cards, as in Texas hold'em.
